note: Manually curated from public news and institutional sources (not automated). Coordinates and radii are approximate — they mark a general area, not an exact boundary. Absence from this list does NOT mean an area is free of enforcement; it means it wasn't specifically documented in the sources checked. enforcement_level reflects reported real-world patrol/fine activity, which is a different question from whether camping is legally banned there (most of Greece is, nationally, since Law 5170/2025 and 5209/2025).

hotspots.name: Sithonia peninsula (Halkidiki)
hotspots.note: Local tourism press reported the 2025 national wild-camping law (5170/2025, refined by 5209/2025) landing hard here specifically, with active local enforcement against camper vans on the peninsula's beaches.

hotspots.name: Peloponnese coastline (general)
hotspots.note: Reported case of motorhome owners fined €300 each while parked by the sea in the Peloponnese, early 2025, under the new national law. This is a broad, approximate area covering the whole peninsula's coast — not a single beach.

hotspots.name: Zakynthos National Marine Park (Laganas Bay: Sekania, Dafni, Gerakas)
hotspots.note: Sea-turtle nesting beaches patrolled directly by National Marine Park rangers; camping and fires are explicitly banned and fines are enforced. Sekania beach is accessible only by licensed boat or ranger escort.

hotspots.name: Elafonisi / Balos / Preveli (Crete)
hotspots.note: Natura 2000 dune/lagoon systems historically popular with backpacker tent camping. Rangers are now present in season, camping and fires are banned, and €300 fines are reported as increasingly enforced.

hotspots.name: Kyparissia Bay / Voidokilia / Gialova Lagoon (Messinia)
hotspots.note: Legally protected Natura 2000 loggerhead turtle nesting habitat, with camping banned under a 2018 presidential decree — but conservation groups (MEDASSET, 2023 Bern Convention review) report that enforcement of that decree has been largely absent. Legally off-limits and ecologically sensitive either way; just don't mistake low patrol activity for it being allowed.
